summary: Episode ep_028 (EP28) shows Juliana seized in the Duchess's bedchamber after a herbarium falls from her pocket and is stepped on by Catherine. Catherine accuses her of poisoning. The Dowager Duchess rises weakly, declares Juliana innocent and says she was poisoned and that Rupert and Catherine knew. The Duchess then collapses, and Juliana is dragged away. Catherine seizes Juliana's locket, reads the herbarium's inscription 'Juliana Ashcroft', exposes Juliana's past, and orders her taken to the wet cells beneath the south tower. Uncertainty: the on-screen evidence never shows the poisoning, the poison, or any antidote. Whether Juliana is guilty is never shown. The Blond Nobleman is never named on screen; his identity as Rupert is inferred from the Duchess's address to Rupert and the scene staging, not stated directly. The guard is unnamed. The metadata logline and continuity note (including the claim that Episode 27 precedes this and the mention of Rupert's order to seize Juliana) are not on-screen evidence and were not used for any event claims. Event timestamps are taken from the supplied scene record and the scene runs 0-138500 ms.

characters.name: Juliana
characters.role: Accused maid; on screen revealed as Lady Juliana Ashcroft, daughter of a disgraced family, and claims to have discovered the poison

characters.name: Catherine
characters.role: Antagonist who frames Juliana, seizes her locket and herbarium, and reveals her identity

characters.name: Rupert
characters.role: Nobleman, likely the Blond Nobleman (identity inferred, not directly named on screen); son of the Dowager Duchess; orders Juliana seized and dragged away

characters.name: Dowager Duchess
characters.role: Bedridden matriarch who defends Juliana, claims she was poisoned, and accuses Rupert and Catherine of knowing

characters.name: Guard
characters.role: Unnamed armed guard who restrains Juliana

beats.description: Guard drags Juliana toward the doorway; the herbarium falls from her pocket and Catherine deliberately steps on it.
Catherine mocks Juliana and accuses her of being a poisoner with herbs and a secret medicine.
Juliana denies poisoning the Duchess; the Blond Nobleman threatens to extract the truth.
The Dowager Duchess wakes, calls Rupert to stop, and declares Juliana innocent and that she saved her.
The Duchess claims she was poisoned and accuses Rupert and Catherine of knowing.
The Duchess collapses and coughs violently; Juliana tries to reach her but is restrained.
Rupert and the Blond Nobleman dismiss the Duchess as mentally damaged by poison.
Catherine and Rupert move to remove Juliana, ordering her taken away before she poisons the house.
Catherine rips the silver locket from Juliana's neck and flings it across the corridor floor while Juliana cries out.
Catherine picks up the herbarium, reads the inscription 'Juliana Ashcroft', and names her Lady Juliana Ashcroft.
Catherine taunts Juliana about her disgraced past and marriage to a penniless war veteran; Juliana protests.
Juliana is ordered to the wet cells beneath the south tower; Catherine holds the herbarium threatening the gallows, and the scene cuts to black.
